title: Resolution: same species or number; only living faith actually justifies
source_text: XLIX. Sed ad mentem eorum penitius intelligendam, in memoriam revocandum est illos docere quidem fidem vivam & charitate formatam esse eundem specie habitum cum informi & mortua fide: imo eandem numero fidem ex mortua vivam, & ex viva mortuam successive fieri posse: sed tamen eos non negare quin fides viva mortuam superet perfectione, saltem externa & accidentali, per quam una ab altera merito distinguitur. Deinde illos quoque communi consensu fateri solam fidem vivam atque efficacem posse hominem actu servare & justificare, illam vero quae mortua & otiosa manet salutem hominis nihil promovere, neque quicquam facere ad hominem justificandum. Adeoque longe plurimi Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores loca illa ubi salus & justitia fidei tribuitur, de fide viva & formata exponenda esse contendunt, & ad eam solam referenda, ut supra fuit a nobis observatum. Quod si qui dicant fidem nondum formatam ad justitiam hominem disponere, & esse justitiae & salutis initium, fundamentum & radicem, per fidem nondum formatam non intelligunt fidem otiosam & mere speculativam, sed fidem quandam actuosam, quae incipit esse per bona opera efficax, quaeque charitatem quodammodo parturit, licet illam adhuc non sit plene adepta, ut patet ex iis quae supra ex Stapletono & Vasquez citata sunt.
pass_a_gloss: But for understanding their mind more deeply, it must be recalled that they do teach living faith formed by charity to be the same species of habit as unformed and dead faith — indeed that the same numerical faith can successively become living from dead and dead from living — yet they do not deny that living faith surpasses dead by a perfection at least external and accidental, by which one is deservedly distinguished from the other. Next they also by common consent admit that only living and efficacious faith can actually save and justify a person, while that which remains dead and idle advances a person salvation not at all and does nothing toward justifying him. And so by far most Roman Doctors contend that those places where salvation and justice are attributed to faith are to be expounded of living and formed faith and referred to it alone, as we observed above. And if any say not-yet-formed faith disposes a person to justice and is the beginning, foundation, and root of justice and salvation, by not-yet-formed faith they do not understand idle and merely speculative faith, but a certain active faith that begins to be efficacious through good works and somehow gives birth to charity, even if it has not yet fully attained it, as is clear from what was cited above from Stapleton and Vasquez.
pass_b_english: Rome holds living formed faith the same species (even same number) as dead, yet living surpasses by external accidental perfection; only living efficacious faith actually saves and justifies.
Salvation-texts they refer to living formed faith; not-yet-formed as disposition means active faith beginning to work and birth charity, not idle speculation (Stapleton; Vasquez).

lemmas.gloss: by a perfection at least external and accidental

choices.why: Same-number possible; still only living actually justifies.
